It must accept `rules` (a list of predicate/_MeterConfig pairs) and `default_config` as keyword-only constructor parameters. Each call to `get_meter()` must invoke the configurator with the meter's InstrumentationScope to determine whether the resulting meter is enabled.

*   When a meter configurator raises an exception during get_meter(), MeterProvider must log at ERROR level and fall back to the default (enabled) configuration for that meter.

*   MeterProvider must expose a `_set_meter_configurator(*, meter_configurator)` method. Calling it must update the stored configurator, re-apply it to all existing meters, and cause all subsequently created meters to use the new configurator. When the configurator raises during re-evaluation of existing meters, MeterProvider must log at ERROR level and keep the meter enabled.

*   Meter must expose a `_is_enabled() -> bool` method that returns the current enabled state of the meter (determined by the most recently applied configurator result).

*   When a meter is disabled, all synchronous instrument operations (counter add, up-down counter add, histogram record, gauge set) must silently skip sending measurements to the measurement consumer.

*   When a meter is disabled, all asynchronous instrument callbacks (observable counter, observable gauge, observable up-down counter) must not invoke their registered callback functions.

*   A meter that starts enabled and is later disabled (via _set_meter_configurator) must immediately stop forwarding measurements for all instruments already created on that meter. A meter that is subsequently re-enabled must resume forwarding measurements.

*   A _get_meter_configurator() function must be added to opentelemetry.sdk._configuration that reads and returns the OTEL_PYTHON_METER_CONFIGURATOR environment variable value (or None if unset).

*   A _import_meter_configurator(meter_configurator_name) function must be added to opentelemetry.sdk._configuration. If the name is None or empty it returns None. ## Summary

I implemented per-meter enable/disable control for the OpenTelemetry Python metrics subsystem, mirroring the existing tracer pattern. Changes across 6 source files (+ CHANGELOG):

**`util/instrumentation.py`** — Added `_scope_name_matches_glob(glob_pattern)` returning an `fnmatch`-based predicate over `InstrumentationScope.name`.

**`trace/__init__.py`** — Removed `_scope_name_matches_glob` and the now-unused `fnmatch` import (it's no longer importable from `opentelemetry.sdk.trace`). The trace configurators still work with the moved helper.

**`metrics/_internal/__init__.py`**
- `_MeterConfig` — dataclass, `is_enabled: bool = True`, `default()` classmethod.
- `_ProxyMeterConfig` — wraps a `_MeterConfig`, exposes `is_enabled` property, `update(config)` swaps the underlying config in place (so all instruments holding the proxy see changes immediately).
- `_default_meter_configurator` / `_disable_meter_configurator` / `_RuleBasedMeterConfigurator` (keyword-only `rules`/`default_config`, first-match-wins).
- `Meter` — accepts optional `meter_config`, stores a `_ProxyMeterConfig`, exposes `_is_enabled()` and `_set_meter_config()`; passes the proxy to every instrument it creates.
- `MeterProvider` — keyword-only `_meter_configurator` param (defaults to `_default_meter_configurator`), stored as `_meter_configurator`; `_apply_meter_configurator` logs ERROR + falls back to default on exception; `get_meter` invokes the configurator on each call; `_set_meter_configurator(*, meter_configurator)` re-applies to all existing meters.

**`metrics/_internal/instrument.py`** — `_Synchronous`/`_Asynchronous` accept `meter_config` and gain `_is_enabled()`. Counter/UpDownCounter/Histogram/Gauge skip forwarding when disabled; async `callback()` returns early (fires no user callbacks) when disabled.

**`environment_variables/__init__.py`** — Added `OTEL_PYTHON_METER_CONFIGURATOR`.

**`_configuration/__init__.py`** — Added `_get_meter_configurator()` and `_import_meter_configurator()` (loads from the `_opentelemetry_meter_configurator` entry-point group, WARNING + None on failure); updated `_init_metrics` (keyword-only `resource`/`exporter_args_map`/`meter_configurator`) and `_initialize_components` (auto-discovers and passes the configurator through).

Verified end-to-end: enabled meters forward measurements and fire callbacks; disabling via `_set_meter_configurator` immediately stops both for already-created instruments; re-enabling resumes; meter identity is preserved; and both error-fallback paths keep meters enabled.
